import parse
from decimal import Decimal

# Edge case tests for R1 - dt_format_to_regex with various format codes
print('R1 edge cases:')
patterns = [
    '%Y',  # Year
    '%m',  # Month
    '%d',  # Day  
    '%H:%M:%S',  # Time
    '%f',  # Microseconds
    '%z',  # Timezone
    '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f %z',  # Full datetime
]
for fmt in patterns:
    try:
        p = parse.dt_format_to_regex(fmt)
        print(f'  {fmt} -> OK')
    except Exception as e:
        print(f'  {fmt} -> ERROR: {e}')

# Test that Parser.formatter returns a copy (not the same object)
p = parse.compile('{a:f}')
f1 = p.formatter
f2 = p.formatter
assert f1 is not f2, 'formatter should return copies'
print()
print('R3 - formatter returns copy: PASS')

# Test hyphen field names work with complex types
p = parse.compile('{my-field:n}')
r = p.parse('1_000')
assert r['my-field'] == 1000, f'Expected 1000, got {r[\"my-field\"]}'
print('R5 - hyphen field name with n type: PASS')

# Test extract_format works correctly
from parse import extract_format
result = extract_format('.5f', {})
print(f'R5 - extract_format(.5f): {result[\"type\"]}, width={result[\"width\"]!r}, precision={result.get(\"precision\", \"N/A\")!r}')
